record.original_question: For every graph G whose adjacency matrix is nonsingular, with maximum degree Delta and minimum degree delta, must the graph energy satisfy E(G) >= Delta + delta, with equality only for complete graphs?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 21 (Akbari-Hosseinzadeh [3]). For every graph with maximum degree Δ and minimum degree δ whose adjacency matrix is non-singular, E(G) ≥ Δ + δ and the equality holds if and only if G is a complete graph.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix A(G). The energy of G is defined as
  E(G) = sum_{i=1}^{n} |λ_i|,
where λ_1, …, λ_n are the eigenvalues of A(G). Let Δ(G) and δ(G) denote the maximum and minimum vertex degrees of G, respectively. Assume that A(G) is nonsingular (i.e., 0 is not an eigenvalue of A(G)).

Prove or disprove: for every such graph G,
  E(G) ≥ Δ(G) + δ(G),
with equality if and only if G is a complete graph.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture has been verified for several restricted graph classes (including regular graphs, bipartite graphs, planar graphs, threshold graphs, triangle-free graphs, and quadrangle-free graphs), but it remains open in full generality. It is still listed as an open conjecture in recent surveys of unsolved problems in spectral graph theory.

status_evidence.title: Validity of Akbari's Energy Conjecture for Threshold Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Validity of Akbari's Energy Conjecture for Threshold Graphs
status_evidence.claim: Verified for threshold graphs, indicating the conjecture is still being attacked class by class.

status_evidence.title: A Lower Bound for Graph Energy in Terms of Minimum and Maximum Degrees
status_evidence.snippet: Proves E(G) >= Delta + delta for regular, bipartite, planar and additional special graph classes.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results confirm the conjecture for several families of nonsingular graphs.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Spectral Graph Theory
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture appears in a recent compilation of unsolved problems.
